# The write direction

4210 rows: one per corpus case, encoding and byte order. 18 systems: one column each, and every cell links to a file. **A cell is never blank** — a blank reads as agreement, and most of the holes in a cross-implementation matrix are not agreements. The words are:

| word | what it means |
|---|---|
| `bytes` | the system ran and these are the octets it produced |
| `same` | it read those octets back and got the case's own sample |
| `different` | it read them back and got something else, which is a defect wherever it appears |
| `refused` | it ran and would not take the type or the value; the link carries its own sentence |
| `unwritten` | nothing to read, because the write direction produced nothing |
| `=` | this row's run *is* the linked encoding's run: a foreign `--encoding` selects the encoding **version**, and the framing follows the type's extensibility |
| `no xcdr2` | the system has no encoding version 2 at all — Fast CDR 1.0.24 has none and CORBA CDR predates XTypes |
| `one order` | the system writes one byte order and this is the other one |
| `no form` | the construct has no form in this system's type model, so its front end never saw the case |
| `no probe` | the toolchain exists and no probe in this tree drives it |
| `not measured` | expressible, a harness in this tree produces it, and no run is recorded |

A cell that carries `w` and a number is one whose **front end said something** about the type — that many distinct warnings, linking to the file that holds them. It is a column of its own and not a note beside a refusal, because the row it matters most in is the one where nothing went wrong. [`WARNINGS.md`](WARNINGS.md) has every warning text, its case count, what it means, and which of them changes what a row below says.

Columns 3 and 4 link to the case's own IDL and sample; the twelve after them to that system's result; then what differs, and the setting that reproduces it. `SYSTEMS.md` says what each column is and which of them a machine without a licensed toolchain can reach.
